source_text: XXI. Ἀχθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ μετὰ σπουδῆς εἰς τὸ στάδιον διὰ τὸ πρόθυμον τῆς πίστεως καὶ ἐπιστάντος τοῦ κομμενταρησίου ἑκὼν ἀπεδύσατο. εἶτα κατανοήσας τὸ ἁγνὸν καὶ δύσχημον τοῦ σώματος ἑαυτοῦ πολλῆς ἐπλήσθη χαρᾶς, ἀναβλέψας δὲ εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ εὐχαριστήσας τῷ τοιοῦτον αὐτὸν διατηρήσαντι θεῷ ἥπλωσεν ἑαυτὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ ξύλου καὶ παρέδωκε τῷ στρατιώτῃ [πεῖραν — obscure; sense: yielded himself for the nailing] τοὺς ἥλους. καθηλωθέντι δὲ αὐτῷ πάλιν ὁ δημόσιος εἶπεν· Μετανόησον καὶ ἀρθήσονταί σου οἱ ἧλοι. ὁ δὲ ἀπεκρίθη· ᾔσθόμην γὰρ ὅτι [εἰσίν — object lost in scan], καὶ συννοήσας ὀλίγον εἶπεν· Διὰ τοῦτο σπεύδω ἵνα θᾶττον ἐγερθῶ, δηλῶν τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν. ἀνώρθωσαν οὖν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ ξύλου, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα καὶ πρεσβύτερόν τινα Μητρόδωρον τῆς αἱρέσεως τῶν Μαρκιωνιστῶν. ἔτυχεν δὲ τὸν μὲν Πιόνιον ἐκ δεξιῶν, τὸν δὲ Μητρόδωρον ἐξ ἀριστερῶν, πλὴν ἀμφότεροι ἔβλεπον πρὸς ἀνατολάς. προσενεγκάντων δὲ αὐτῶν τὴν ὕλην καὶ τὰ ξύλα κύκλῳ περισωρευσάντων ὁ μὲν Πιόνιος συνέκλεισε τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς, ὥστε τὸν ὄχλον ὑπολαβεῖν ὅτι ἀπέπνευσεν. ὁ δὲ κατὰ τὸ ἀπόρρητον εὐχόμενος ἐλθὼν ἐπὶ τὸ τέλος τῆς εὐχῆς ἀνέβλεψεν. ἤδη δὲ τῆς φλογὸς αἰρομένης γεγηθότι προσώπῳ τελευταῖον εἰπὼν τὸ ἀμὴν καὶ λέξας· Κύριε, δέξαι μου τὴν ψυχήν, ὡς [ἡδέως — scan dosvyousvos] ἡσύχως καὶ ἀπόνως ἀπέπνευσε καὶ παρακαταθήκην ἔδωκε τὸ πνεῦμα τῷ πατρὶ τῷ πᾶν αἷμα καὶ πᾶσαν ψυχὴν ἀδίκως κατακριθεῖσαν ἐπαγγειλαμένῳ φυλάξαι.
pass_a_gloss: With him brought in haste into the arena because of the readiness of faith, and with the jailer attending, of his own will he stripped; then observing the chaste and wasted state of his own body he was filled with much joy, and looking up into heaven and giving thanks to God who had kept him so, he stretched himself on the timber and yielded to the soldier for the nails, the sense being for the nailing; and with him nailed the executioner said again, Repent and your nails will be removed, and he answered, For I perceived that [object lost], and after brief reflection he said, For this I hasten that I may rise more quickly, signifying the resurrection from the dead; then they set him upright on the timber, and after this also a certain elder Metrodorus of the sect of the Marcionists; and it happened that Pionius was on the right and Metrodorus on the left, but both looked toward the east; and with them bringing up fuel and heaping timbers round in a circle, Pionius closed his eyes, so that the crowd supposed that he had expired; but praying in the hidden manner and coming to the end of the prayer he looked up; and with the flame already rising, with rejoicing face saying at last the amen and uttering, Lord receive my soul, as [text uncertain] quietly and without pain he breathed his last and gave his spirit as a deposit to the Father who promised to guard every blood and every soul unjustly condemned.
pass_b_english: They brought him in haste into the arena, for his faith was eager, and while the registrar stood by he stripped of his own will.

Then seeing how chaste and how wasted his own body had become, he was filled with great joy, and looking up to heaven and thanking God for keeping him so, he laid himself out on the timber and gave himself to the soldier for the nailing.

Once the nails were in him the executioner said again, “Repent, and your nails will be taken away.” He answered, “For I have perceived it,” though what he perceived is lost, and after thinking a little he said, “That is why I hasten, so that I may rise the sooner,” meaning the resurrection from the dead.
So they raised him upright on the timber, and afterwards they raised a certain elder Metrodorus of the Marcionist sect as well.
It so happened that Pionius was on the right and Metrodorus on the left, yet both faced east.
When the men had brought the fuel and piled the wood in a circle around them, Pionius closed his eyes, so that the crowd thought he had already died.
But he was praying in the hidden way, and when he reached the end of the prayer he looked up.

With the flame already rising, his face rejoicing, he spoke the final amen and said, “Lord, receive my soul” (Acts 7:59), and then, quietly and without pain, he breathed his last and gave his spirit as a trust into the keeping of the Father, who promised to guard every drop of blood and every soul unjustly condemned.

lemmas.gloss: led/brought, here under escort into the arena
stretched out, laid himself flat for nailing
nailed down, dative absolute after nailing
will be taken away, future passive promise
rise sooner, aorist subjunctive of resurrection
set upright, raised the nailed timber
heaped around, piled wood in a circle
with rejoicing face, dative of manner
unjustly condemned, perfect passive sense here

choices.why: Latin loan commentariensis, the prison officer attending the execution, not a general commentator.
Substantive for the public slave who does the nailing and urges recantation in context.

choices.term: τὸ ἁγνὸν καὶ δύσχημον τοῦ σώματος
choices.english: the chaste and wasted state of his body
choices.why: δύσχημον here describes unsightly emaciation from prison, paired with ἁγνὸν as moral purity preserved.
ξύλον is the stake/cross-beam for nailing and burning, not a living tree.
